Here's a rephrased version of the text:

Furthermore, video games are increasingly being recognized for their therapeutic benefits, moving beyond their reputation as mere forms of entertainment. Meanwhile, research by McGonigal (2012) suggests that games like "SuperBetter," which incorporate psychological concepts, can have a profound impact on mental health. Not only can they help alleviate symptoms of anxiety and depression, but they can also aid in the recovery process from physical trauma. Additionally, these games tap into the principles of positive psychology, harnessing the potential of video games to empower players to take an active role in their own healing. Moreover, by incorporating elements of social support, cognitive training, and emotional regulation, these games can provide a unique and effective therapeutic experience. And, ultimately, this growing recognition of video games' therapeutic potential has the potential to revolutionize the way we approach mental health treatment.
